decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left approach to the left tube, lifting while orienting toward its visible cap-to-tip axis; right arm remains home.
Advance left above the tube while continuing the down-facing grasp orientation, using small continuous increments.
Finish orienting the open left gripper over the left tube and descend to a conservative pregrasp height.
Wrist view shows a lateral and angular offset; correct the open gripper toward the tube and align its long axis before closing.
Center the tube between the left fingers with a small capward correction, then close while stationary.
Lift the first tube clear of the tabletop with the gripper held closed; inspect retention before transport.
Retention is visible. Rotate the first tube toward upright while moving it toward the rack's left side, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Complete the upright rotation above the left rack slots, keeping the tube closed in the gripper and clear of the rack.
Lower the upright first tube toward the left-front rack hole with a small rightward alignment correction; keep hold until seated.
Continue a straight slow insertion into the aligned left rack opening, keeping the tube upright and the gripper closed.
The tube appears supported at the slot but contact shifted it in the fingers. Open without further pushing, then retreat slightly to inspect whether it settles upright.
The released first tube is leaning rather than fully seated. Approach its body with the open left gripper aligned to the lean for a corrective grasp.
Attempt to recapture the displaced first tube and lift it clear for visual reassessment before another insertion.
The recaptured tube is held nearly along the gripper approach axis. Lift clear and begin rotating that axis downward to restore a vertical tube.
Move the recovered tube inward above the left rack opening, preserving its current grip while checking the visible tip alignment.
Make a small visual alignment correction and gently lower the recovered tube into the left opening.
The tip appears on the near rim. Shift slightly rearward and right into the opening before another short insertion.
Release above the aligned opening to allow gravity seating, then clear the rack for an unobstructed inspection.
Clear the first tube and allow it to settle into the visible opening. Retract the left arm while beginning an elbow-up right approach to the far-right tube.
The first tube did not remain in the rack and is now on the right tabletop. Continue with the isolated far-right tube, keeping the left arm clear and returning it toward home.
Bring the open right gripper down-facing above the isolated tube; finish a gradual left return without crossing workspaces.
Use the wrist view to center the right tube and move the grasp slightly toward its cap while descending to pickup height.
Correct the remaining right-wrist lateral offset, then close around the tube body without translating.
Lift the right-hand tube clear with a closed grip, retaining its orientation before transport toward the rack.
Transport the retained right tube inward while gradually rotating it upright, keeping clearance above the table.
Continue the smooth inward transport and upright rotation of the retained tube, staying on the rack's right side.
Finish bringing the tube upright over the rack's right large opening; pause above contact for visual alignment.
Correct the right tube slightly left toward the large slot and lower halfway to contact while maintaining an upright closed grasp.
Lower into the visually aligned right-front opening slowly, correcting the remaining small tilt and watching for tube motion relative to the fingers.
Contact shifted the tube upward. Relieve pressure and shift rearward-right off the rim, then open gently to let the upright tube settle.
Withdraw the open right fingers away from the released tube and inspect whether gravity seats it in the rack.
The released tube remains upright in the right slot. Clear it safely and begin the next right-side tube approach.
Orient the open right gripper toward the front tube's diagonal axis while approaching from above; the first inserted tube remains untouched.
Finish the down-facing orientation over the next tube and approach pickup height with the fingers open.
Align the next tube's long axis and center its body in the right fingers, then close at pickup height.
Lift the newly grasped tube clear and slightly back, keeping the grip closed before rotating toward an unoccupied rack slot.
Carry the retained second tube toward the central empty slot while gradually rotating upright, clear of the occupied right slot.
Continue upright rotation and transport toward the central opening, holding the tube securely above the rack.
Complete the upright pose above the central empty opening, maintaining clearance from the seated right tube.
Lower the second tube toward the central slot along a vertical path, correcting a small residual tilt.
Advance the upright second tube slowly into the central slot, watching for rim contact or slippage before releasing.
The second tube is supported but has slid in the fingers. Release without further force and withdraw to inspect its seating.
The central tube has settled upright. Retract the open right hand clear of both seated tubes before approaching the last tube on the right tabletop.
Approach the final tabletop tube from the right, rotating the open gripper toward its diagonal axis while leaving both seated tubes clear.
Continue the open right approach and gradual down-facing rotation toward the last tube, staying clear of the rack.
Complete the down-facing orientation and correct rightward toward the last tube's visible body before closing.
The last tube is diagonal in the wrist view. Rotate the open gripper to its actual axis and make a small capward centering correction.
The tube axis is now aligned but left of the fingers. Center the open gripper laterally, then close around its body.
Lift the final tube clear with a closed right grip, leaving the two seated tubes undisturbed; verify retention before transport.
Carry the last retained tube toward an empty rear slot from the right, gradually turning it upright while remaining above the seated tubes.
